MRE:

```python
from typing import Generic, TypeVar, TypeGuard

class A: ...
class B: ...

def is_a(_: object) -> TypeGuard[A]: return True
def is_b(_: object) -> TypeGuard[B]: return True


_T = TypeVar("_T")

class Foo(Generic[_T]):
    def __init__(self, v: _T) -> None:
        if not is_a(v) and not is_b(v):
            raise ValueError
        self.v = v
```

One type guard is not enough, union is necessary for this crash. Since we started narrowing tvar upper bounds, such logic in constructor can create typevars with TypeGuard/TypeIs in their upper bounds.
Downgrading mypy to `1.16.1` fixes the issue for me

issue.title: Prevent TypeGuardedType leak from `narrow_declared_type` as part of typevar bound
issue.body: Fixes #20015, refs #18895 as a previous example of the same issue. I don't see any similar problems in other branches.
